newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia prime minister to start coalition talks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia prime minister to start coalition talks.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, whose Liberal Democrats (LDS) won the most votes in a general election two weeks ago, will start coalition talks late on Wednesday, his party said.

The centre-left Liberal Democrats won 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats but face a loose alliance of rightists, known as the "Spring" parties, which together gained 45 seats, just one seat short of an absolute majority.
"Tonight Drnovsek will meet presidents of the Spring parties," LDS general secretary Gregor Golobic, told a news conference. The meeting would be closed to the public, he added.
"We expect the meeting to give us an answer as to whether we can talk about a coalition at all and to be a foundation for more concrete talks in the future," Golobic said.
Drnovsek, 46, who has served as prime minister since 1992, could have a battle on his hands returning to power as premier, political analysts have said.

The Spring alliance, comprising the conservative People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats is pushing for Marjan Podobnik, 35, head of the People's Party, to become the next prime minister.
Podobnik's pro-farmer party won 19 seats, the biggest share among the Spring parties. The alliance has offered LDS a place in government if Drnovsek steps down as premier.
But the LDS has said it would only cooperate in a government where Drnovsek was prime minister.
Golobic of the LDS said the key question was not how to win the 46 votes in parliament necessary to elect a prime minister, but how to form a stable government.
He said Drnovsek would also hold coalition talks with other parliamentary parties in the next couple of days.
President Milan Kucan must name a candidate for premier within 30 days of the first session of the new parliament, set for November 28.
